one_liner: Batched QR, Cholesky and unpivoted LDL^T solves for thousands of small matrices in interleaved layout; beats per-matrix LAPACKE and matches or beats MKL compact.
what_it_does: A C API (cbk.h) of LAPACK-named routines with a _compact suffix: ?geqrf, ?ormqr, ?orgqr, ?potrf/?potrs/?posv, ?sytrfnp/?sytrsnp/?sysvnp, ?trsm and ?gels, in s and d. Each call factors or solves a whole pool of same-sized small matrices stored in the compact (interleaved) format, where element (i,j) of V consecutive matrices sits side by side and V (2, 4, 8 or 16) is passed explicitly. The portable API has no pack/unpack helpers, so you write your data in that layout yourself (the index formula is in cbk.h). An optional MKL-style layer (-DCBK_WITH_MKL=ON) adds cbk_?*_compact entry points that take MKL_COMPACT_PACK and mix with MKL's own compact routines and pack/unpack, filling the routines MKL's Compact API does not have (apply/form Q, Cholesky and LDL^T solves, gels).
how_it_is_fast: It uses SIMD across matrices instead of within one: V independent factorizations run in lockstep, one vector lane per matrix, so small n never starves the vector unit and no lane masks are needed. The kernels are vectorized unblocked LAPACK algorithms (geqr2 with a branch-free larfg, potf2, a square-root-free potf2 for LDL^T, a register-tiled blocked LDL^T update), written once with GNU vector types and lowered to SSE, AVX or AVX-512. The fused drivers (?posv, ?sysvnp, ?gels) factor and solve each group of V matrices while it is still in cache instead of streaming the pool through separate passes. OpenMP threads the loop over groups.
when_to_use: Thousands of independent same-sized dense systems of order roughly 8-120 (per-element FEM/DG blocks, small least-squares fits, Kalman updates, batched local solves) on x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512
You already use MKL's Compact API (mkl_?geqrf_compact, mkl_?potrf_compact) and need the missing pieces: apply/form Q, a Cholesky or LDL^T solve, or a one-call batched gels
SPD or diagonally dominant / well-behaved symmetric indefinite systems, where unpivoted Cholesky or LDL^T is numerically safe
One-RHS or few-RHS solves: the gels win over per-matrix LAPACKE_dgels is 2.7x geomean at nrhs=1 and narrows to 1.3x at nrhs=64
You want a dependency-free library (only CMake >= 3.28 and a C++17 GCC/Clang) that you can build with -march=native
when_not_to_use: Matrices of order above about 128: per-matrix LAPACK pulls ahead from roughly n=128-168 (0.25x at n=256 for the SPD solve) because the compact kernels are unblocked
Matrices that need pivoting: there is no column-pivoted QR, the LDL^T is unpivoted (no Bunch-Kaufman), and rank deficiency or a non-SPD input is not reported (that lane silently becomes Inf/NaN)
Badly scaled or ill-conditioned inputs: there is no LAPACK dlarfg-style overflow/underflow rescaling (listed as a known limitation)
Mixed sizes, complex numbers or GPUs: one size per call, real s/d only, CPU only

Production code that needs a long track record: v0.2.0 (2026-09-15), 1 star, mostly written by Claude models with human review per the README, and the API is still changing (0.2.0 broke ?ormqr's signature)

integration.form: static lib (shared with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON); CMake package cbk::cbk
integration.dependencies: none for the library (OpenMP optional); tests need LAPACKE + CBLAS (OpenBLAS, Netlib, Accelerate via accelerate-lapacke, or MKL); benchmarks and the MKL-style API need Intel MKL
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 GCC or Clang (GNU vector extensions; icpx also handled), CMake >= 3.28; tested with GCC and Clang on x86-64 Linux, plus a macOS CI job
integration.platforms: Any target GCC/Clang can lower vector types for (SSE, AVX, AVX-512, non-x86 extensions per the CHANGELOG); performance documented only on an unnamed AVX-512 x86-64 machine
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant (state is caller-owned); each routine forks an OpenMP team over groups only when there are at least two groups and enough work, and runs serially when called from inside a caller's parallel region unless nested parallelism is enabled; results do not depend on the thread count
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: names and argument orders follow LAPACK and MKL compact, but the data must be in compact interleaved layout; the MKL-style layer is a true drop-in companion to MKL's compact routines, not a replacement for per-matrix LAPACKE calls

gotchas: Build with -march=native (or an explicit -m flag): the library sets no -march, so a default build emits baseline SSE2 while MKL dispatches AVX-512 at runtime. Building from your own build system also needs -fno-math-errno, or the vector square root turns into scalar libm calls.
Workspace is not checked: an undersized lwork in the MKL-style compact routines is an out-of-bounds write, and under MKL's threaded layer MKL's own ?geqrf_compact sizes its workspace per thread.

Align buffers to 64 bytes: unaligned bases still work but cost up to ~40% on small sizes. Issue #34 (clang 18 with AVX segfaulting on 16-byte-aligned buffers) was closed by PR #35, and cbk.h now says the loads and stores never fault.

The upper-triangle LDL^T convention is A = U^T D U, the transpose of LAPACK ?sytrf's A = U D U^T. The docs also disagree on the OpenMP gate (cbk.h says about 2e5 flops, threading.md and building.md say 5e4).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick cbk over BLASFEO when you have many independent small systems of one size to factor or solve at once; BLASFEO speeds up one small matrix at a time (panel-major, chained operations such as Riccati recursions) and offers more of BLAS/LAPACK. The small-GEMM siblings (LibShalom, IAAT) cover only matrix multiply, not factorizations.
verified_claims_summary: First-party, labelled 'indicative', on a '4-core AVX-512 container' (CPU model not named), gcc -O3 -march=native, sequential MKL for its compact kernels and LAPACKE, all paths given the same thread count, and pack/unpack not timed. One-call gels was 2.7x faster than LAPACKE_dgels (geomean over n=10..120, 1000 matrices, 1 RHS; 1.3x at 64 RHS), and the open three-step chain beat MKL's compact chain by 1.12-1.25x. The fused SPD solve ran 2-9x faster than LAPACKE_dposv at orders 8-48 and only matched MKL's compact pipeline (0.9-1.0x geomean).
status_note: Actively developed (v0.2.0 released 2026-09-15, 316 commits, one open feature issue for rank-revealing QR) and Apache-2.0, so it is copyable. It is young, has a single maintainer, and the CHANGELOG lists testing only on x86-64 Linux against Intel MKL 2020.4.
